tldr: Azure Monitor’s metrics-usage insights are now generally available, giving you a way to find unused metrics and investigate workspace consumption.
MiniMax says its new M3.1 Flash model cuts agent costs by 70%; validate that claim against your own multi-call workloads before updating forecasts.
OpenCode users should check for exposed API keys and unexpected usage after attackers accessed part of its online platform.

top.title: Azure Monitor metrics-usage insights reach general availability
top.summary: Metrics usage insights are generally available for Azure Monitor workspaces, showing utilization, unused metrics, usage trends, and changes driving consumption.
top.why: Use it to identify metrics you can stop collecting and to investigate what is driving workspace usage before changing monitoring budgets.

top.title: Azure DNS can link record sets directly to Traffic Manager
top.summary: Azure DNS now supports DNS-based load balancing through direct links between DNS record sets and Traffic Manager profiles, removing the need for a CNAME pointing to the profile.
top.why: Revisit DNS designs that use Traffic Manager: the direct association may simplify record management, but check how it fits your existing failover and routing setup.

top.title: MiniMax says M3.1 Flash cuts AI-agent costs by 70%
top.summary: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash, a faster, cheaper update to its M3 model, and says it reduces the cost of running AI agents by 70%. The report does not provide independent validation of that figure.
top.why: Benchmark it on your own agent workflows before revising forecasts, since repeated model calls can make per-task cost differ from headline claims.

top.title: Microsoft adds controls for agents that may act like insider threats
top.summary: Microsoft introduced security controls that restrict what an AI agent can do as its assessed risk rises, addressing the danger of agents having excessive access to enterprise systems.
top.why: When designing agent access, plan for permissions that can be limited as risk changes rather than giving an agent broad, persistent access.

also.title: US orders DeepSeek removed from federal civilian agencies
also.summary: The Department of Homeland Security ordered DeepSeek technology removed from federal civilian agencies, citing security risks and potential access to government infrastructure.

also.title: Samsung is expanding semiconductor capacity to meet memory demand
also.summary: Samsung’s Pyeongtaek complex has three fabs operating and a fourth coming online as demand grows for the specialized memory used alongside AI GPUs.

also.title: AI agents reportedly helped a hacker break into more than 100 websites
also.summary: A security firm says a hacker used mostly autonomous AI agents to breach over 100 websites, with Reuters reporting John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins among the victims.

top.title: Attackers stole API keys from AI coding tool OpenCode
top.summary: Attackers accessed part of OpenCode’s online platform and stole some users’ API keys, then used AI services in ways that ran up charges.
top.why: If your team uses OpenCode, check for exposed keys, rotate them, and review provider billing for unexpected usage.
